ruling.recommended_action: Refund $5.08 (1 non-exempt segment × 3.60 km × $1.4100/km) to the rider as a Ryde voucher under the NS-7 framework; no account flag — RD-6's predicate (a prior upheld route dispute in 90 d) is absent on this record.
ruling.reasoning:
This is a metered RydeTAXI trip, so distance driven feeds the fare and the detour branch of RD-2 applies: refund = Σ(extra_km of non-exempt segments) × this trip's per-km rate [F4][F7][RD-2]. The rate is the fare record's distance fare ÷ distance km: $41.06 ÷ 29.12 km = $1.4100/km (the trace fixes $1.4100; 4.17 km × $1.4100 = $5.88, matching the billed excess-distance figure) [F4][F7][RD-2].

One off-route segment is measured: 15:21–15:30, 6.32 km driven where the optimal route covers 2.71 km, +3.60 km, diverging up to 1425 m [F1][F2][F3][RD-1]. No traffic incident on the replaced stretch is recorded, so RD-4 gives no exemption for it [F15][RD-4].

The only rider message before the segment is Chat #2 at 15:18: "Just take whichever way is faster lah, I'm late." [F8][F9][F10]. That is an authorisation of a route chosen to reach the destination, not of an errand or loop of the driver's own [RD-5]. The record does not settle whether the segment driven was that faster route: the driver proposed avoiding the Pan Island Expressway (band-2 congestion, confirmed by the traffic fact), but a speed band alone does not exempt [F8][F12][RD-4], and the fact table carries no road name for the driven path — no stop on the agreed road, no message placing the car on it — so nothing ties the segment to the route the rider authorised [RD-5][G13]. The rider's complaint that it "wasn't faster at all" cannot be verified from the record, and the driver's after-the-trip statement that the rider agreed verbally is a claim, not consent [F11][RD-5]. Timing satisfies the "before the segment" requirement [F9], but scope is undetermined: the words can be read as covering a route that genuinely avoids the congestion (exempt) or as not covering a loop that was not that route (counts). Because this finding changes the amount, the case cannot be decided on the record and goes to a person [RD-5][RD-2].

RD-3 gives no exemption: no stop was measured in this segment and no rider message named a place the car stopped at [F3][F8][F9][RD-3]. RD-6's predicate is absent — the driver has 0 upheld route disputes in the last 90 days — so no account flag arises; profile facts cannot decide the case either way [F17][F18][RD-6]. The $0.11 waiting fee is metered waiting time, which RD-3(c) leaves charged on RydeTAXI [F5][F7][RD-3].

Safety screen: I read the complaint, both chat messages and the driver's statement. There is no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation — only a route and fare dispute [F8][F9][F11][RD-1]; safety_concern = none.

If the segment is treated as non-exempt, the amount is 3.60 km × $1.4100/km = $5.076 → $5.08 [F3][F4][RD-2]; the residual 0.57 km of the measured +4.17 km excess is not attributed to any segment and is not refunded [F4][RD-2].
